{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 19 playbook rules. The agreement is unusually strong for us: 17 of 19 rules are compliant, including the critical indemnification and IP/Customer Data positions, and the high-severity assignment, licence grant, termination-for-convenience, exclusivity and non-compete positions. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, MFN obligation or non-solicitation covenant binding us, and several provisions (§ 7.6 vendor-granted MFN, § 12.4 vendor competition restraint, § 22.3 audit findings as our Confidential Information, § 11 transition pricing) run affirmatively in our favour.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory rather than merely below the fallback:

- **§ 21.1 liability cap (critical).** The cap is measured against "Fees" as defined in §§ 1.5–1.6 — the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee in the first Order Form — and § 21.1 further confines recovery to that first Order Form. The cap is illusory and far below six months' fees. The remainder of § 21 is at our preferred position (mutual cap, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims in § 21.3 that include indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security breaches), so a single edit to the cap basis resolves the issue.
- **§ 7.7 liquidated damages (high).** The agreement imposes liquidated damages on us of 15% of annual Fees for **each week** an invoice is late — triggered by a minor payment delay and capable of exceeding remaining contract value within weeks. This fails the fallback, which permits only a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

No findings are recorded as missing. Subject to these two edits, we see no other barrier to signature.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence (with §§ 14, 15) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## 3. Deviations and proposed redlines

### 3.1 § 21.1 — Liability cap basis (critical)

**What changed and why.** We reset the cap basis to **the greater of the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms, including subscription fees, in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and USD 1,000,000.** As drafted, the cap keys off the § 1.5–1.6 definition of "Fees" (the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee in the first Order Form) and is further confined to that first Order Form, which leaves us with no meaningful recovery. Our playbook position is a claim-anchored twelve-month lookback on a "fees paid or payable" basis; we deliberately use lowercase "fees" so the narrow § 1.5 definition is not re-imported, and we do not broaden to "all amounts". §§ 21.2 and 21.3 are untouched — the mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the uncapped Excluded Claims (which already place the Vendor indemnity outside the cap, better than our 3× super-cap fallback) remain as drafted.

### 3.2 § 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages (high)

**What changed and why.** We replaced the § 7.7 formula with an unconditional statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties. A 15%-of-annual-Fees charge per week of late payment is punitive and can exceed remaining contract value; our playbook permits only a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, and no such fee exists elsewhere (§ 9.4 requires only accrued Fees with a refund of prepaid Fees, and § 27 termination is expressly "without penalty"). The balance of § 7 — including the withholding and interest mechanics in § 7.3 — is unchanged.

---

## 4. Walk-away items

Both deviations are identified in our findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** A cap measured against the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and confined to the first Order Form is far below six months' fees and fails the fallback on a material term.
2. **§ 7.7 — punitive Customer-payable liquidated damages.** 15% of annual Fees per week of invoice delay is outside anything our playbook permits us to accept.

No other finding reaches walk-away territory.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Issue the two-clause redline** to Vendor (§ 21.1 cap basis; § 7.7 deletion and replacement) with the playbook rationale above. These are the only changes we require.
2. **Hold the line on both.** Each is a walk-away item; we should not trade one for the other, and we should resist any attempt to reopen §§ 21.2–21.3, which we are leaving untouched.
3. **Confirm no drafting knock-on** from the § 21.1 edit — in particular that the lowercase "fees" formulation is preserved on turn-back so the narrow § 1.5 definition is not reintroduced.
4. **Record the noted-but-not-flagged points** in the deal file for future renewals: the § 14.1 Customer Data processing right extends to "improve the Services for Customer"; § 13.2 permits contractor support rather than a general sublicence; the § 24.2 competitor bar is consent-gated rather than absolute; the § 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code intentionally introduced by Vendor; and the § 19.4 refund arises only after Vendor fails to cure within a reasonable period. None of these warrants a redline now.
5. **Request certificates of insurance** under § 18.2 at signature, and diarise the § 8.2 thirty-day non-renewal window and the Vendor sixty-day renewal reminder.
6. **Route for signature** once the two edits are accepted."}
